elements.element: The clause must use either the mutual-agreement renewal pathway or the automatic-renewal pathway.
elements.evidence: The clause uses the automatic-renewal pathway: it renews automatically for additional one-year periods.

elements.element: If the mutual-agreement renewal pathway is used, renewal must require mutual written agreement.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the clause instead uses automatic renewal.

elements.element: If the automatic-renewal pathway is used, each renewal term must be 12 months.
elements.evidence: The clause provides for automatic renewal for “an additional one year period” on each anniversary.

elements.element: If the automatic-renewal pathway is used, Customer must be able to opt out on 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Either Party, which includes Customer, may prevent renewal or terminate by giving 30 days' written notice.

elements.element: If the automatic-renewal pathway is used, Vendor must give Customer a renewal reminder 60 days before each renewal.
elements.evidence: The operative addition requires HDI to give the Company written notice of each upcoming renewal 60 days before the renewal date.

elements.element: If the automatic-renewal pathway is used, renewal-period price increases must be capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that any renewal-period price increase may not exceed the lesser of CPI and 3%.
The clause expressly provides for automatic renewal on each anniversary.

elements.element: The automatic-renewal non-renewal notice window must be no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: The operative notice period is 30 days, which is no more than 60 days.

elements.element: Renewal-period price increases must not exceed 5%.
elements.evidence: The lesser-of-CPI-and-3% cap cannot exceed 3% and therefore cannot exceed 5%.

result.reason: The operative language satisfies the preferred automatic-renewal alternative and therefore also satisfies the fallback. It is not fully minimal because changing the shared notice period from 90 to 30 days also gives Vendor a 30-day termination right, whereas the preferred position requires only Customer's 30-day opt-out. The notice provision is also framed as a general termination right rather than expressly as notice of non-renewal, but it still enables Customer to prevent renewal on 30 days' notice. No unrelated term is displaced or new contradiction introduced.
